kind: Frozen parent interpretation for narrow independent counterreview; static evidence only

claims.claim: SaveManager.Start registers an instance-bound Clean UnityAction on the current LoadManager.onPreSceneChange event. Zero raw direct Clean xrefs is therefore not a no-caller proof.
claims.limit: Registration path in native bytes, not observation of successful listener installation/order/invocation in every runtime.

claims.claim: Clean locally clears Saveables +0x48 and BaseSaveables +0x50. It does not locally drain Completed +0x60, requests +0x68 or reset SaveManager.IsSaving +0x29. It is not an own-participant last-use acknowledgement.
claims.limit: Local body claim only; does not rule out other cleanup elsewhere or prove what live requests survive.

claims.claim: On its loaded exit path LoadManager invalidates IsGameLoaded and ActiveSaveInfo, sets its own IsLoading, then starts the exit coroutine. PreSceneChange is invoked later by that coroutine, so that event is not a reliable place to recover the already-cleared old active identity.
claims.limit: Only the locally shown successful path/order. No universal event delivery, EH or transitive callback claim.

claims.claim: The server branch of exit yields a fixed 1.25-second realtime wait. The client branch requests Player data, then WaitUntil uses Player.Local.playerSaveRequestReturned OR realtime elapsed > maxWait (3 seconds). Neither shown wait is a SaveManager request/batch/completed drain or a last-use acknowledgement for the own business.
claims.limit: No multiplayer acceptance or correctness analysis of player network save itself. Timeout alone does not prove request success.

claims.claim: SaveManager.Awake calls the shared PersistentSingleton<SaveManager>.Awake body, which first calls Singleton.Awake and, unless duplicate-marked, detaches its transform and calls DontDestroyOnLoad on its GameObject. A menu scene load is therefore not by itself evidence that this manager or all of its references die. Singleton.OnDestroy merely conditionally nulls its own static instance; it supplies no save-drain logic.
anchors: 0x5A8FEB: persistent base call with SaveManager MethodRef
claims.limit: No assertion that every live manager survives or that Unity engine persistence is reimplemented here. Open-generic FieldMap offsets can be unresolved/zero; no inference uses those offsets.

claims.claim: ConfirmExitScreen.ConfirmExit and Tools.ExitToMenu.Exit directly call ExitToMenu with null autoLoadSave/popup and preventLeaveLobby=false; no local SaveManager drain check is present. ConfirmExitScreen.Update formats time-since-save, not a drain proof. Exit may call StartGame for a captured autoLoadSave after Menu; StartGame publishes new current save info/folder before its load coroutine later invokes PreSceneChange and CleanUp. Current singleton/path is not immutable old-request ownership.
claims.limit: No claim that every UI caller is inventoried, every UI interaction is enabled while saving, or any observed world was corrupted. StartGame rejects an already loaded world; no unsafe direct slot-switch claim is made. LoadManager.CleanUp is separate from SaveManager.Clean; not a save-drain acknowledgement.

claims.claim: The selected SaveRoutine.Dispose body is ret 0 plus padding and has no own completion/cleanup acknowledgement. StopAllCoroutines is a cached indirect Unity internalcall wrapper; its engine implementation and actual cancellation/dispose behavior remain unanalysed. No complete negative abort or terminal-completion proof follows from these windows or the raw E8/E9 scan.
claims.limit: Shared Dispose target is not a proposed hook. Raw xrefs are candidates; only six are confirmed in the new windows. Indirect calls, delegates, external modules, EH and Unity destruction/cancellation semantics are not completely covered.

claims.claim: Combined with the independent own-lifecycle source review, no verified own last-use/removal/world-exit boundary exists for a transient business save participant. Keep fail-closed before registration/save. Close this audit with a bounded architecture decision: do not turn the synchronous transient probe into an async writer by simply removing the guard. Prefer a separately designed own operation owner with frozen identity/revocation and explicitly proven participant lifetime/non-retarget/non-IO behavior, or obtain a complete transient detach proof first. Neither alternative is implemented or approved.
claims.limit: A reasoned design requirement, not a native implementation theorem. Retain, an own callback counter, a persistent root, Idle, Completion, queue emptiness or one later frame does not substitute for last-use proof. Own release, native save success and sidecar consistency remain three distinct proof goals.
